events.headline: Madrigal initiates pivotal Phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH trial of resmetirom in biopsy-confirmed NASH with fibrosis
events.detail: The company began enrolling patients with biopsy-confirmed NASH and stage 2-3 fibrosis into a three-arm, placebo-controlled trial of 80 mg and 100 mg resmetirom, with a week-52 liver biopsy in the first cohort intended to support a possible accelerated-approval filing.

source.title: Form 10-K for fiscal year 2019 (quoting the company's March 28, 2019 trial-initiation announcement)

events.opened_note: Used the 10-K, which quotes the March 28, 2019 announcement verbatim, because the original 2019 press release/8-K exhibit for this specific announcement could not be located and opened directly.

events.headline: Madrigal opens a second pivotal trial, MAESTRO-NAFLD-1, for enrollment in a related NASH population
events.detail: The company opened for enrollment a 52-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study of resmetirom in about 700 patients with NASH and presumed NASH, intended to add safety and metabolic data alongside MAESTRO-NASH.

source.title: Form 10-K for fiscal year 2019 (quoting the company's December 10, 2019 announcement)

events.opened_note: Same 10-K as e1; original December 2019 press release not independently opened.

events.headline: Company says COVID-19 site-safety measures let its two Phase 3 trials continue without protocol changes
events.detail: In response to regulatory guidance during the early pandemic, Madrigal put COVID-19 safety measures in place at MAESTRO-NASH and MAESTRO-NAFLD-1 trial sites and said both studies were able to continue without protocol modification; connection to this business: pandemic-era site access and travel restrictions were an industry-wide risk to enrollment and monitoring at clinical-trial sites.
events.opened_note: 10-K states the company announced these measures 'in April 2020' without giving the specific calendar day; date approximated to 2020-04-01.

events.headline: Madrigal completes enrollment of the 900-patient liver-biopsy population in MAESTRO-NASH
events.detail: The company reached its planned enrollment target for the 52-week liver-biopsy portion of MAESTRO-NASH (900 patients, at least 450 at fibrosis stage 3) and said it expected to report topline 52-week biopsy results by the third quarter of 2022.

source.title: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals Completes Enrollment of the 52 Week Liver Biopsy Patient Population in the Phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH Study of Resmetirom

events.headline: Pivotal Phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH meets co-primary NASH-resolution and fibrosis-improvement endpoints
events.detail: Both the 80 mg and 100 mg doses of resmetirom were statistically superior to placebo on NASH resolution (26% and 30% vs. 10%) and on at least one-stage fibrosis improvement (24% and 26% vs. 14%); the company said it intended to file for accelerated approval in the first half of 2023.

source.title: Madrigal Announces Positive Topline Results from the Pivotal Phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH Clinical Trial of Resmetirom for the Treatment of NASH and Liver Fibrosis

events.headline: FDA grants Breakthrough Therapy designation for resmetirom as the trial's outcomes-portion enrollment completes
events.detail: The designation was supported by the 52-week biopsy results reported in December 2022; the company also completed enrollment of the roughly 1,750-patient outcomes portion of MAESTRO-NASH and said its planned NDA filing remained on track for the second quarter of 2023.

source.title: Madrigal Receives Breakthrough Therapy Designation from FDA for Resmetirom and Completes Enrollment of the Phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH Biopsy Trial

events.headline: Madrigal begins rolling submission of its NDA seeking accelerated approval of resmetirom
events.detail: The company said it had submitted the majority of the New Drug Application to the FDA, with the remaining components to follow in July 2023, using the rolling-review process enabled by the April 2023 Breakthrough Therapy designation, and requested priority review.

source.title: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals Announces Rolling Submission of New Drug Application to U.S. FDA Seeking Accelerated Approval of Resmetirom for the Treatment of NASH with Liver Fibrosis

events.headline: FDA accepts the resmetirom NDA, grants Priority Review, and sets a March 14, 2024 PDUFA date
events.detail: The FDA accepted the application for review under the accelerated-approval pathway and assigned a target action (PDUFA) date of March 14, 2024; the agency said it was not currently planning to hold an advisory committee meeting.

source.title: Form 8-K (Item 8.01, Other Events): FDA acceptance and Priority Review of the resmetirom NDA

events.headline: Madrigal prices a $500 million stock offering to fund launch preparations ahead of the FDA decision
events.detail: The company priced 1,248,098 shares of common stock plus pre-funded warrants for 2,048,098 shares at $151.69 per share, for expected gross proceeds of about $500 million, saying proceeds would go toward clinical and commercial activities in preparation for a potential resmetirom launch.

source.title: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals Announces Pricing of $500 Million Public Offering

horizon_notes.1: By the one-year mark (2023-11-13 minus four years, i.e. 2019-11-13), the company had launched its primary pivotal trial, MAESTRO-NASH, in March 2019 and opened a second Phase 3 study, MAESTRO-NAFLD-1, for enrollment in December 2019 [e1][e2]. No Phase 3 program specific to the related cholesterol-disorder (HeFH) indication was announced in this window. Interpretation: the pre-cutoff packet's open question of whether the regulator would agree to a pivotal-trial design was answered within the year -- the trial launched -- but the packet could not say whether the second, related indication flagged as a possible 2019 catalyst would actually advance; within this window it did not appear as a Phase 3 program.
horizon_notes.3: By the three-year mark (2021-11-13), Madrigal said COVID-19 site-safety measures in 2020 let both ongoing Phase 3 studies continue without protocol changes [e3], and in June 2021 it completed enrollment of the 900-patient liver-biopsy population in MAESTRO-NASH, guiding to topline 52-week results by the third quarter of 2022 [e4]. Interpretation: the packet's central unresolved question -- whether the week-12/week-36 Phase 2 imaging and biopsy signal would replicate in a larger, longer pivotal trial -- remained untested throughout this span, since no pivotal readout had occurred by the three-year mark; a reader relying on the packet alone would still be waiting for the decisive data point.
horizon_notes.5: By the five-year mark (2023-11-13), the record shows the Phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH trial met its co-primary NASH-resolution and fibrosis-improvement endpoints in December 2022 [e5]; resmetirom then received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation in April 2023 [e6], the company began a rolling NDA submission in June 2023 [e7], and the FDA accepted the application with Priority Review and a March 14, 2024 PDUFA date in September 2023 [e8], around the same time Madrigal priced a $500 million stock offering to fund launch preparations [e9]. Interpretation: the packet's central tension -- whether Phase 2 surrogate/biopsy data would survive the field's history of Phase 3 failures, despite high-profile conference placement -- was resolved in the trial's favor inside this window, but the packet could not have told a reader that the FDA's final approval decision would land four months after the five-year coverage window closes, so the approval itself falls outside this record.

aftermath.attribution_caveat: Price moves have many causes; the events here are what was public, not a proof of why the price moved.
gaps: The exact calendar day of the April 2020 COVID-19 site-safety announcement is not stated in the FY2020 10-K; the event date (2020-04-01) is approximated to the start of that month.

No dedicated source was found confirming whether the heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) Phase 3 program flagged as a possible cutoff-era catalyst was formally paused, deprioritized, or simply not prioritized; all post-2019 company disclosures reviewed here describe only the NASH/MASH (resmetirom) liver-disease program.
The FDA's final approval action on the NDA (PDUFA date March 14, 2024) falls after the five-year coverage_end of 2023-11-13 and is out of scope for this timeline.

Several pages on ir.madrigalpharma.com timed out repeatedly and could not be opened directly; SEC EDGAR filings and GlobeNewswire/BioSpace wire copies of the same releases were used instead where available.

scene_check.voice: Their liver-disease drug cut liver fat in a placebo-controlled trial and the biopsies show the disease actually resolving. They just raised close to half a billion, and the plenary slot at the big liver meeting says the field is paying attention.

claims.text: placebo-controlled Phase 2 met its primary endpoint on liver fat
36-week biopsies showed NASH resolution and fibrosis improvement
cash and investments of about $488 million after a June stock sale

debrief_check.s1: The regulator agreed and the pivotal trial launched in March 2019; it met both co-primary endpoints in December 2022 [e1][e5].
debrief_check.s2: Replicated in Phase 3. Breakthrough designation followed in April 2023, the NDA was accepted with priority review in September 2023, and the approval decision fell four months after this five-year window [e6][e7][e8].
debrief_check.s3: Enough to get there, with another $500 million stock sale in September 2023 to fund the launch [e9]. Compare with the five-year return in the tiles: the science the friend described was right, and the price at the cutoff had already paid for most of it.

assumptions.text: The Phase 2 biopsy results will replicate in a large Phase 3.
The regulator will agree a trial design that this drug can pass.
Cash is enough to reach the readout without a dilutive raise.
Even if the drug works, five years is too long for the price to reward it.
I don't have enough evidence to take a position either way.

thesis_check.a1: Evidence: the 900-patient Phase 3 met both co-primary endpoints, NASH resolution and fibrosis improvement, in December 2022 [e5]. For this assumption: supported, four years after the cutoff. Unknown: the size of the benefit against the field's history; the record has the outcome, not the effect sizes.
thesis_check.a2: Evidence: the pivotal trial started in March 2019 and a second in December 2019; enrolment of the biopsy population completed in June 2021 [e1][e2][e4]. For this assumption: supported within the first year. Unknown: what the regulator asked for in the design; the record shows only that the trial launched.
thesis_check.a3: Evidence: the company reached the readout and the filing, then sold $500 million of stock in September 2023 to fund the launch [e7][e8][e9]. For this assumption: right to the readout, wrong after it. Unknown: how much the second raise cost earlier holders; the tiles show the five-year return.
thesis_check.a4: Evidence: approval came four months after the five-year window closed [e8]; the shares over five years are in the result tiles, against a market that rose strongly. For this assumption: supported in the sense that the science being right did not pay inside the horizon. Unknown: what a six-year holder saw.
thesis_check.a5: Evidence: nothing decisive happened for four years, then the trial won and the stock still lagged the market over five [e4][e5]. For this assumption: fair, and the record rewarded neither buying nor shorting much. Unknown: this is one drug; the field's base rate is not in the record.
